metadata.title: Why Tesla, Google, and other Mag 7 stocks are losing billions in valuation

content.text:
Yahoo Finance Markets and Data Editor Jared Blikre takes a closer look at stock valuation losses from Tesla (TSLA), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Meta (META), Amazon (AMZN), and Microsoft (MSFT).
We have uh about $750 billion in losses for certain members of the Mag 7 and I have a bunch of tickers here and I'm might say, well, what's the rhyme and reason behind this? I'm going to tell you because if I sort by performance, maybe you're going to start to see a pattern. So the losers here, Tesla down 19% for the week. Of course, they announced earnings and it was a big disappointment, not on the top line number. They're making more cars than ever and they're pulling in more money than ever, but profits, profitability is suffering.
Alphabet had a kind of a the opposite problem. They are increasing their margins. Uh they're basically spending more money, but they're also making more money. However, their cash flow went negative for the first time going back to their IPO. So over 20 years, they have never been cash flow negative, now they are.
Amazon and meta, guess what? They are reporting next week and I think they're just down in sympathy. Same for Microsoft here. So we got some big earnings on deck for next week. But then what explains all this green up here? You're going to know Super Micro up 25%, uh looks like digital realty up 16% and uh Super Micro announced some really big numbers this week and they are on the opposite end of some of these hyper scalars like Alphabet because they are receiving money through the AI trade instead of spend instead of having to spend it.
Same for digital realty Trust up 16%. They're spending their own money too, but they have leases that are locked in. They are the owners of the data centers. That is a good business to be in right now.
Dell is up 9%, Western Digital up seven, Micron up about 6 and a half, Seagate, very similar. even Nvidia. So it wasn't all the uh it wasn't all the Mag 7 that were down this week. Nvidia as a chipmaker, as a recipient of this uh capex money, they are up 1%. So, if you take a look at who was losing the most money this week and who gained the most money, I think this pretty well encapsulates it.
And again, we're looking forward to next week. We got four huge earnings. I didn't mention Apple. They're kind of the odd uh Mag 7 out and that's because they don't have very big capex expenses and that is currently working in their favor. They just had a huge day today and they are back towards record highs. They are a standout whereas a lot of these other Mag 7 are just kind of uh sinking right now.
